submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires retrospectively when the current token completes a conventionalized local collocation ('defendant pleaded', 'O(n', dosage '500 mg', 'Once upon', 'cat sat', 'market fell'), with peak strength graded by how tightly the preceding token or tokens predict it: swapping either half of the bigram for a non-formulaic alternative collapses the peak, while swapping only the upcoming token leaves it identical. Neither half alone drives it ('pleaded' after 'He' is 0.13 versus 4.43 after 'defendant'; 'sat' after 'dog' is 0.09 versus 0.51 after 'cat'), and the weak sub-0.7 bumps on common bigrams versus multi-point peaks on rare formulas reflect its two SwiGLU regimes; the Jacobian G/g output direction has no behavioral counterpart (pole ablation KL far below 1e-3 with no consistent upcoming-G effect), so no lookahead is claimed.
